title: project.init request
description: Create a project document set from chosen source files. `prepared_output`: `prepare` reports the plan and writes nothing, `commit_reviewed` re-derives it and writes only if the digest still matches. Refuses outright when a project already exists at the destination — there is no replace, because the root-last write ordering that makes an interrupted init safe only holds for a fresh set. The destination is named here rather than by the envelope's `project` locator, because the project does not exist yet.

name.description: The project's display name. Its id is derived from this.

destination.description: Where the project is created, as an identity the adapter resolves against its own output root. Never a host path.

sources.description: The files to register, as identities the resolver resolves. Each becomes a source with its size and digest pinned, and a whole-file object — an object with no selector would verify as unrecoverable.

media.description: `copy` puts each source under the project's `original/` directory, making the project self-contained. `in_place` leaves it where it is: under the root it gets a project-relative location, outside it a `.amiga-re/local.json` binding that is true on this machine only. There is no third option, because a source with neither verifies as unbound next session.

maximum_input_bytes.description: Per-source ceiling. The aggregate ceilings — source count, total input bytes — are the context's and are not request-settable, because they exist to bound what a caller asks for.
